kcs.label: Intensity: très, trop, assez, un peu
kcs.description: Adverbs that grade an adjective or adverb: très (very), trop (too), assez (quite/enough), un peu (a bit), pas très (not very). Trop means excessive, not 'very'. Beaucoup is used with verbs, not adjectives.
forms: très + adjective: très grand
trop + adjective: trop cher (too expensive)
assez / un peu / pas très + adjective
verb + beaucoup: J'aime beaucoup… (not *très aime)

examples.fr: Ce pantalon est trop petit pour moi.
examples.en: These trousers are too small for me.

examples.fr: Le film est très drôle, j'aime beaucoup.
examples.en: The film is very funny; I like it a lot.

mastery: Distinguishes très and trop in heard comments
Grades adjectives in descriptions with très / assez / un peu / trop
Explains in a shop why an item is not suitable (trop grand, pas assez chaud)
commonErrors: (EN) Using trop to mean "very" in a positive sense
(EN) *très beaucoup / *J'aime très le chocolat
boundaries: Quantity adverbs with nouns (beaucoup de) are kt:fr-g-quantity; assez and peu as quantity adverbs at A2 are kt:fr-g-frequency-quantity-adverbs.

primitives.binding: Put pas très – un peu – assez – très – trop on a ladder, then choose a rung for each situation
Judge très/trop/beaucoup in context; classify the error, then write two sentences

kcs.label: Asking about and describing people
kcs.description: Asking who someone is and describing them: identity, job, appearance, character and relation to others (married, brother of, friend of). At A2 descriptions include relationships between people.
forms: Qui est-ce ? / Il est comment ? / Elle est comment ?
Il est grand, mince, brun; elle a les cheveux longs / les yeux bleus
Elle est sympa, gentille, timide, drôle
C'est le frère de… / Ils sont mariés / Elle est la meilleure amie de…
Il porte des lunettes.

examples.fr: Ton prof, il est comment ? – Il est jeune et très sympa.
examples.en: What's your teacher like? – He's young and very nice.

examples.fr: Lucie et Tom sont mariés ; ils ont deux enfants.
examples.en: Lucie and Tom are married; they have two children.

mastery: Identifies a person in a picture from a spoken description
Writes a five-sentence description of a person (appearance and character)
Asks about and describes a friend or celebrity for a partner to guess
commonErrors: (EN) *Il est cheveux longs (avoir les cheveux …)
(EN) *Comment est-il ? answered with job only
(EN) Missing feminine agreement in the description
boundaries: Appearance and character vocabulary is kt:fr-lex-appearance; biography/portrait is kt:fr-fn-biography.

primitives.binding: Group picture: learner describes one person; a checker verifies hair, glasses and clothes against the picture
Guess who: learner asks yes/no questions about appearance to identify a hidden person

kcs.label: Appearance, character and personality
kcs.term: La description physique et le caractère
kcs.description: Words to describe people's bodies and personalities: height, build, hair, eyes, age, and basic character adjectives with their feminine forms.
forms: grand(e), petit(e), mince, gros(se) — prefer fort(e) for politeness
les cheveux blonds / bruns / roux / courts / longs; les yeux bleus / verts / marron (invariable)
jeune, âgé(e), beau / belle, joli(e)
sympa (sympathique), gentil(le), drôle, timide, sérieux / sérieuse, bavard(e), calme

examples.fr: Mon frère a les yeux marron et les cheveux courts.
examples.en: My brother has brown eyes and short hair.

examples.fr: Elle est bavarde mais très gentille.
examples.en: She's talkative but very kind.

mastery: Matches descriptions to portraits
Writes masculine and feminine forms of 15 description adjectives
Describes self and one family member using appearance and character words
commonErrors: (EN) *les yeux marrons (marron is invariable)
(EN) Using gros(se) without realising it can be rude
boundaries: How to build a description is kt:fr-fn-describe-people.
kcs.placementNote: The Inventaire lists this theme under A1 in Annexe F (p. 66) and under A2 in Annexes D and E; introduced at A1 because A1 already requires describing people.

Judge phrases (les yeux marron/marrons, il a les cheveux/il est cheveux); sort errors, write a description

kcs.label: Asking about and describing things
kcs.description: Asking about objects (what, what colour, what size, what it is for) and describing them by colour, size, shape, material and use, typically to buy, find or identify something.
forms: Il est de quelle couleur ? – Il est noir.
C'est grand / petit / lourd / léger / cher
C'est en cuir / en bois / en coton
Ça sert à … (A2) / C'est pour …
Vous avez ce modèle en bleu ?

examples.fr: Je cherche un sac noir, pas trop grand, en cuir.
examples.en: I'm looking for a black leather bag, not too big.

examples.fr: C'est quoi, ce truc ? – C'est pour ouvrir les bouteilles.
examples.en: What's this thing? – It's for opening bottles.

mastery: Identifies an object from a heard description
Describes a lost object in writing (colour, size, material)
Asks a shop assistant for an item by its characteristics

(EN) Forgetting agreement of colour adjectives with feminine nouns
boundaries: Colours and clothes vocabulary are kt:fr-lex-clothes; comparing things is kt:fr-fn-compare.

primitives.binding: Lost-property pictures: learner describes one object; checker verifies colour, size, material

kcs.label: Present tense of regular -er verbs
kcs.description: About 90% of French verbs end in -er and share one pattern: stem + -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Four of the six forms sound the same (parle, parles, parle, parlent), so the subject carries the person in speech. The French present covers both 'I work' and 'I am working'.
forms: je parle, tu parles, il/elle/on parle
nous parlons, vous parlez, ils/elles parlent (-ent silent)
j' before a vowel: j'aime, j'habite
spelling changes: nous mangeons, nous commençons; j'achète, je m'appelle
present = habitual and current action: Je travaille (I work / I'm working).

examples.fr: Le samedi, nous jouons au foot et ils regardent le match.
examples.en: On Saturdays we play football and they watch the match.

examples.fr: J'habite à Lyon et je travaille dans une banque.
examples.en: I live in Lyon and I work in a bank.

mastery: Hears that parle/parles/parlent sound the same and identifies the person from the subject
Conjugates unseen regular -er verbs in all persons in writing
Talks about own week using six different -er verbs
commonErrors: (EN) Pronouncing -ent in ils parlent
(EN) Adding a progressive form for current actions (*Je suis parler)
(EN) *nous mangons (missing e before -ons)
boundaries: Irregular high-frequency verbs are kt:fr-g-present-irregular; être en train de is kt:fr-g-etre-en-train-de.

primitives.binding: Induce the -er endings from parler, then apply them to unseen verbs (danser, voyager); each step shows the stem + ending rule
Hear il parle / ils parlent / nous parlons; judge who acts from audible cues only

kcs.label: Present of high-frequency irregular verbs
kcs.term: Le présent des verbes usuels irréguliers
kcs.description: A short list of irregular verbs used in almost every A1 sentence: aller, faire, prendre, venir, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, mettre, partir/sortir, lire, écrire, boire, voir, plus -ir verbs like finir. Each is learned as a whole paradigm; patterns (stem changes in nous/vous, -s -s -t endings) help.
forms: aller: vais, vas, va, allons, allez, vont
faire: fais, fais, fait, faisons [fəzɔ̃], faites, font
prendre: prends, prends, prend, prenons, prenez, prennent
venir: viens, viens, vient, venons, venez, viennent
finir: finis, finis, finit, finissons, finissez, finissent
partir, sortir, dormir: pars, pars, part, partons, partez, partent

examples.fr: Le matin, je prends le bus et je vais au lycée.
examples.en: In the morning I take the bus and go to school.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que vous faites ce soir ? – Nous sortons.
examples.en: What are you doing tonight? – We're going out.

mastery: Selects the correct form of aller, faire, prendre, venir for each subject
Writes the full paradigm of six core irregular verbs
Describes a daily routine using aller, faire, prendre and partir
commonErrors: (EN) *vous faisez / *vous disez
(EN) Regularising aller (*je alle)
(EN) *ils prendent (missing double n: prennent)
boundaries: Modal verbs pouvoir/vouloir/devoir are kt:fr-g-modals; which verbs are taught at A1 is an editorial choice (see REVIEW.md).

primitives.binding: Verb + person card: produce the form before reveal; first attempts recorded per verb
Group verbs by pattern (partir/sortir/dormir; prendre/apprendre/comprendre) and apply to unseen members

kcs.label: Pronominal (reflexive) verbs in the present
kcs.description: Pronominal verbs have a pronoun that matches the subject: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons, vous vous levez, ils se lèvent. Many daily-routine verbs are pronominal (se réveiller, se laver, s'habiller, se coucher), as are s'appeler and reciprocal verbs (se parler).
forms: me, te, se, nous, vous, se (m', t', s' before a vowel)
se lever, se réveiller, se laver, se brosser les dents, s'habiller, se coucher
s'appeler: je m'appelle, nous nous appelons
negative: Je ne me lève pas tôt.
infinitive: Je vais me coucher.

examples.fr: Je me réveille à sept heures et je me lève tout de suite.
examples.en: I wake up at seven and get up straight away.

examples.fr: Le dimanche, nous ne nous levons pas tôt.
examples.en: On Sundays we don't get up early.

mastery: Matches the reflexive pronoun to the subject in gapped sentences
Places ne … pas correctly around pronoun + verb
Describes a morning routine with five pronominal verbs
commonErrors: (EN) Omitting the pronoun (*Je lève à 7 h)
(EN) Using se for every person (*je se lève)
(EN) *Je me ne lève pas
(EN) *Je lave mes dents for "I brush my teeth" (je me brosse les dents)
boundaries: Pronominal verbs in the passé composé (with être) are kt:fr-g-pc-agreement.

primitives.binding: Slots subject – (ne) – reflexive pronoun – verb – (pas); learner drags blocks and the violated slot is named
Order pictures of a morning routine, then retell with pronominal verbs and d'abord / ensuite

kcs.label: Telling the time and timetables
kcs.term: Demander et donner l'heure, des horaires
kcs.description: Asking and giving the time in everyday (12-hour, with et quart, et demie, moins le quart) and official (24-hour) style, and reading opening hours and timetables.
forms: Quelle heure est-il ? / Il est quelle heure ? – Il est trois heures.
Il est deux heures et quart / et demie / moins le quart / moins dix
midi, minuit
official: 14 h 30 = quatorze heures trente
À quelle heure ? – À 8 heures. / de 9 h à 18 h / Le magasin ouvre à… ferme à…

examples.fr: Il est quelle heure ? – Il est midi et demi.
examples.en: What time is it? – It's half past twelve.

examples.fr: Le train part à dix-sept heures quarante-cinq.
examples.en: The train leaves at 17:45.

mastery: Sets a clock to a time heard in both styles
Writes times in words and figures (14 h 30)
Finds opening hours on a sign and arranges a meeting time
commonErrors: (EN) *Il est trois heures et demi(e) confusion with midi et demi
(EN) Saying *moins quinze in 12-hour style (use moins le quart)
(EN) Omitting heures (*Il est trois)
boundaries: Numbers are kt:fr-lex-numbers-0-69; à + time is in kt:fr-g-time-prepositions.

primitives.binding: Station announcements and phone messages: write departure times into slots; errors classed by 12/24-hour style
Opening-hours signs and a bus timetable: find the one time needed for a task

kcs.label: Days, months, seasons, dates and holidays
kcs.term: La date, les jours, les mois, les saisons, les fêtes
kcs.description: Calendar vocabulary and how to say a date: le + cardinal number + month (le 14 juillet), except le premier for the 1st. Days and months are written without capitals. Includes main French holidays.
forms: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche
janvier … décembre; le printemps, l'été, l'automne, l'hiver
au printemps, en été, en automne, en hiver
Nous sommes le combien ? / On est quel jour ? – On est le 3 mai.
le premier janvier; Noël, le jour de l'An, Pâques, le 14 Juillet

examples.fr: Mon anniversaire, c'est le premier avril.
examples.en: My birthday is on the first of April.

examples.fr: Le lundi, je travaille ; le samedi, je me repose.
examples.en: On Mondays I work; on Saturdays I rest.

mastery: Writes dates heard in random order
Says dates with le + number + month and le premier
Asks and answers about birthdays and holiday dates
commonErrors: (EN) Capitalising days and months
(EN) *le un mai / *le deuxième mai
(EN) *dans l'été / *au été (en été, but au printemps)
(EN) Saying *le lundi when meaning "on Monday" (this coming one: lundi)
boundaries: Prepositions of time (en 2015, à 7 h) are kt:fr-g-time-prepositions.

primitives.binding: Hear dates in invitations and announcements; fill in a calendar; errors by day/month/ordinal
Calendar page → say the date aloud before reveal

kcs.label: Daily activities
kcs.description: Verbs and phrases for an ordinary day: getting up, meals, going to work or school, housework, shopping, going to bed.
forms: se lever, se doucher, s'habiller, prendre le petit déjeuner
aller au travail / à l'école, travailler, étudier, rentrer
déjeuner, dîner, faire la cuisine, faire les courses, faire le ménage
regarder la télé, lire, se coucher
le matin, l'après-midi, le soir, la nuit

examples.fr: Elle rentre à six heures et elle fait les courses.

kcs.label: Talking about habits and schedules
kcs.description: Asking and telling what someone usually does, when and how often, using the present, times and frequency words (le lundi, tous les jours, d'habitude).
forms: Qu'est-ce que tu fais le week-end ? / Tu te lèves à quelle heure ?
d'habitude, tous les jours, le lundi (every Monday), le matin
Je travaille de 9 h à 17 h.
Quand est-ce que tu as cours ? – Le mardi et le jeudi.

examples.en: Do you do sport? – Yes, on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

kcs.label: Prepositions of time: à, en, le, de … à
kcs.description: Prepositions to place an event in time: à + clock time, en + month/year/season (except au printemps), le + date, no preposition before days for a single occasion, de … à / du … au for ranges.

en mai, en 2015, en été (au printemps)
le 3 juin, le lundi (habit), lundi (next Monday)
de 9 h à 17 h, du lundi au vendredi
avant / après le dîner

examples.fr: Je suis né en 2004, le 12 octobre.
examples.en: I was born in 2004, on 12 October.

mastery: Chooses à / en / le / Ø for time expressions

Gives the dates and times of an event in a short message
commonErrors: (EN) *en lundi / *sur lundi
(EN) *de lundi à vendredi (du lundi au vendredi)
boundaries: Durations (depuis, pendant, il y a) are kt:fr-g-time-indicators and kt:fr-g-time-a2.

primitives.binding: Judge time phrases (en mai / *à mai / au printemps / *en printemps); classify by unit of time; write a schedule

kcs.label: Question words
kcs.term: L'interrogation : qui, où, quand, comment, combien, pourquoi
kcs.description: Information questions with qui, où, quand, comment, combien (de), pourquoi and que/qu'est-ce que. Three word orders coexist: question word + est-ce que + S + V (Où est-ce que tu habites ?), S + V + question word in speech (Tu habites où ?), and inversion (Où habites-tu ?).
forms: Qui ? Où ? Quand ? Comment ? Combien (de) ? Pourquoi ? – Parce que …
Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? / Tu fais quoi ? (speech)
Où est-ce que vous habitez ? / Vous habitez où ? / Où habitez-vous ?
Combien de frères tu as ? / Ça coûte combien ?

examples.fr: Tu arrives quand ? – Samedi matin.
examples.en: When are you arriving? – Saturday morning.

examples.fr: Pourquoi est-ce que tu apprends le français ? – Parce que j'aime voyager.
examples.en: Why are you learning French? – Because I like travelling.

mastery: Matches question words to answers
Forms questions with est-ce que and with the word at the end
Interviews a partner with six different question words
commonErrors: (EN) *Où tu habites est-ce que
(EN) *Quoi tu fais ? (quoi only at the end in speech or alone)
(EN) *Combien frères (missing de)
boundaries: Quel is kt:fr-g-quel; yes/no questions are kt:fr-g-yes-no-questions.

primitives.binding: Build questions in three orders from blocks; the system names the slot rule broken
Missing information on a festival poster; learner must ask quand, où, combien to complete it

kcs.label: Quel, quelle, quels, quelles
kcs.description: Quel ('which/what') agrees with the noun it asks about. It is used before a noun (Quel âge ?) or with être (Quelle est ton adresse ?). The four forms sound the same.
forms: quel (m. sg.), quelle (f. sg.), quels (m. pl.), quelles (f. pl.)
Quel âge as-tu ? / Tu as quel âge ?
Quelle est votre adresse ?
À quelle heure ?
Exclamation: Quel beau temps ! (A2)

examples.fr: Quelle est ta couleur préférée ?
examples.en: What's your favourite colour?

examples.fr: Tu prends quel train ?
examples.en: Which train are you taking?

mastery: Chooses the written form of quel that matches the noun
Asks for address, age, nationality with quel
Completes a form interview using quel questions
commonErrors: (EN) Using qu'est-ce que for "what is your…" (*Qu'est-ce que est ton nom ?)
(EN) Not agreeing quel in writing
boundaries: Exclamative quel is kt:fr-g-exclamation.

primitives.binding: Questions where only quel/quelle/quels shows which noun is asked about
Partner has a profile; learner asks quel/quelle questions to fill nationality, age, address

kcs.label: Asking for and giving information
kcs.description: Getting practical information (opening times, location of facilities, prices, availability) from staff or passers-by, and at A2 giving such information to others.
forms: Où sont les toilettes, s'il vous plaît ?
Le musée est ouvert le lundi ?
Il y a un distributeur près d'ici ?
Je voudrais des renseignements sur …
giving: C'est ouvert de… à… / C'est au premier étage.

examples.fr: Excusez-moi, le musée ferme à quelle heure ? – À dix-huit heures.
examples.en: Excuse me, what time does the museum close? – At six pm.

examples.fr: Je voudrais des renseignements sur les cours du soir.
examples.en: I'd like some information about evening classes.

mastery: Understands the key information in a short answer from a clerk
Asks three practical questions at an information desk
Gives a visitor directions to facilities and opening times
commonErrors: (EN) Asking with a bare noun and no opener (Toilettes ?), which sounds abrupt
(EN) Forgetting the opener and s'il vous plaît
boundaries: Directions in the street are kt:fr-fn-directions; explanations and precise clarification are kt:fr-fn-explanation.

primitives.binding: Tourist office: learner needs opening times, price and location held by the partner
Information desk with branching answers (closed, full, other floor)

kcs.label: The weather
kcs.description: Talking about weather with impersonal il fait / il y a / il pleut / il neige, temperatures, and understanding a very simple forecast.
forms: Quel temps fait-il ? – Il fait beau / mauvais / chaud / froid / doux.
Il pleut. Il neige. Il y a du vent / du soleil / des nuages.
Il fait 20 degrés.
la pluie, la neige, l'orage, le ciel
forecast: demain, il va pleuvoir; nuageux, ensoleillé

examples.fr: Aujourd'hui, il fait beau mais il y a du vent.
examples.en: Today it's nice but windy.

examples.fr: Il pleut ? Prends ton parapluie !
examples.en: Is it raining? Take your umbrella!

mastery: Matches weather phrases to symbols on a map
Describes today's weather in two sentences
Picks the key information (rain, temperature) from a short radio forecast
commonErrors: (EN) *C'est chaud for the weather (il fait chaud)
(EN) *Il est pleuvant
(EN) Using être for temperature (*Il est 20 degrés)
boundaries: Seasons are kt:fr-lex-dates.

primitives.binding: Short forecasts: fill a grid of city × weather × temperature
Weather map: learner describes three regions; checked against symbols

kcs.label: Asking about and giving news of people
kcs.term: Demander, donner des nouvelles de quelqu'un
kcs.description: Asking how someone not present is doing and giving short news (health, work, location, family events).
forms: Comment va ta mère ? / Et ton frère, ça va ?
Il va bien / Elle va mieux / Il est malade.
Elle habite toujours à … / Il travaille maintenant à …
Donne-lui le bonjour de ma part. / Embrasse-la pour moi.

examples.fr: Et tes parents, ils vont bien ? – Oui, très bien, merci.
examples.en: And your parents, are they well? – Yes, very well, thanks.

examples.fr: Ma cousine habite toujours à Lyon ; elle a un bébé maintenant.
examples.en: My cousin still lives in Lyon; she has a baby now.

mastery: Understands short news about third persons in a dialogue
Asks after two family members of a friend
Gives two pieces of news about a friend or relative
commonErrors: (EN) *Comment est ta mère ? meaning "how is she" (comment va…)
(EN) Using être for health (*Elle est bien) where aller is expected
boundaries: Talking about one's own state of health is kt:fr-fn-physical-state.

primitives.binding: Meeting a neighbour: ask about family members; responses branch (ill, moved, new baby)
Transfer the phrases to news about the learner's own family

kcs.label: Talking about likes and preferences
kcs.description: Expressing likes, dislikes and preferences with aimer, adorer, détester, préférer, followed by a noun with the definite article or by an infinitive.
forms: J'aime / J'adore / Je n'aime pas / Je déteste + le/la/les + noun
J'aime + infinitive: J'aime nager.
Je préfère … / Tu préfères le thé ou le café ?
J'aime bien (I quite like) vs J'aime (I like/love; with people: I love)
Moi aussi / Moi non plus / Pas moi

examples.fr: J'adore le cinéma mais je n'aime pas les films d'horreur.
examples.en: I love cinema but I don't like horror films.

examples.fr: Tu préfères la mer ou la montagne ? – Je préfère la montagne.
examples.en: Do you prefer the sea or the mountains? – I prefer the mountains.

mastery: Ranks heard opinions from adorer to détester
Writes four likes and dislikes with the definite article
Compares preferences with a partner using moi aussi / moi non plus
commonErrors: (EN) *J'aime chocolat / *J'aime du chocolat
(EN) Saying Je t'aime bien vs Je t'aime without knowing the difference
(EN) *J'aime à nager
boundaries: Articles are kt:fr-g-articles; what pleased in the past (ça m'a plu) is kt:fr-fn-evaluate.

primitives.binding: Place détester – ne pas aimer – aimer bien – aimer – adorer on a ladder, then pick a rung for each item
Find a partner with the same three likes by asking Tu aimes … ?

kcs.label: Leisure and sports
kcs.description: Names of hobbies and sports and the verbs that go with them: faire de + sport/activity (faire du vélo, de la natation), jouer à + game/sport (jouer au foot), jouer de + instrument (jouer du piano).
forms: faire du sport / du vélo / de la danse / de la natation / du yoga
jouer au foot / au tennis / aux cartes / aux jeux vidéo
jouer du piano / de la guitare
aller au cinéma / à la piscine / au concert
lire, dessiner, cuisiner, se promener

examples.fr: Le week-end, je fais du vélo et je joue de la guitare.
examples.en: At weekends I go cycling and play the guitar.

examples.fr: Ma sœur joue au basket deux fois par semaine.
examples.en: My sister plays basketball twice a week.

mastery: Sorts activities into faire de / jouer à / jouer de
Writes sentences about hobbies with correct contractions (du, au)
Talks about own leisure time and asks a partner
commonErrors: (EN) *jouer le piano / *jouer le foot
(EN) *faire le vélo / *faire de le vélo
(EN) *Je fais natation
boundaries: Contractions (au, du) are in kt:fr-g-place-prepositions and kt:fr-g-partitive.

primitives.binding: Sort activities into faire de / jouer à / jouer de boxes, induce the rule, then handle exceptions
Pictures of people doing activities; learner says who does what; checked against the picture

kcs.label: Modal verbs: pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir + infinitive
kcs.description: Pouvoir (can/may), vouloir (want), devoir (must/have to) and savoir (know how to) are followed directly by an infinitive. Pouvoir is ability or permission in a situation; savoir is a learned skill. All four are irregular.
forms: pouvoir: peux, peux, peut, pouvons, pouvez, peuvent
vouloir: veux, veux, veut, voulons, voulez, veulent
devoir: dois, dois, doit, devons, devez, doivent
savoir: sais, sais, sait, savons, savez, savent
modal + infinitive: Je peux venir. Tu veux manger ? Il doit partir. Elle sait nager.
negative: Je ne peux pas venir.

examples.fr: Je ne peux pas sortir ce soir, je dois travailler.
examples.en: I can't go out tonight; I have to work.

examples.fr: Tu sais nager ? – Oui, mais je ne veux pas aller à la piscine.
examples.en: Can you swim? – Yes, but I don't want to go to the pool.

mastery: Chooses pouvoir or savoir for "can" in context
Conjugates the four modals in gapped sentences
Refuses an invitation giving a reason with je ne peux pas / je dois
commonErrors: (EN) *Je peux nager for a learned skill (je sais nager)
(EN) Adding de or à (*Je veux de partir)
(EN) *Je ne peux venir pas
boundaries: Il faut is kt:fr-g-il-faut; polite je voudrais is kt:fr-g-conditional-politeness; expressing obligation at A2 is kt:fr-fn-obligation.
The Inventaire lists devoir, pouvoir, vouloir in Annexe E and adds savoir in its Annexe F examples.

primitives.binding: Same picture, different intent (ability, permission, wish, obligation); learner picks the modal and sees how the meaning shifts
Apply the four modal paradigms in new sentences; the system shows the stem changes

kcs.label: Inviting, accepting and refusing
kcs.description: Making and responding to invitations and offers, accepting with thanks or refusing politely with an excuse.
forms: Tu veux venir … ? / Tu es libre samedi ? / Ça te dit de … ?
Avec plaisir ! / D'accord ! / Bonne idée ! / Merci, c'est gentil.
Désolé(e), je ne peux pas. Je dois … / Je suis pris(e).
offering: Tu veux un café ? – Oui, je veux bien. / Non merci.

examples.fr: Tu veux venir dîner samedi ? – Avec plaisir, merci !
examples.en: Do you want to come to dinner on Saturday? – With pleasure, thanks!

examples.fr: Désolée, je ne peux pas, je travaille ce soir.
examples.en: Sorry, I can't, I'm working tonight.

mastery: Identifies acceptances and refusals in heard replies
Writes a short invitation message with day, time and place
Accepts one and refuses one invitation politely with a reason
commonErrors: (EN) Answering Tu veux un café ? with just *Oui (add je veux bien / merci)
(EN) Refusing without excuse or thanks, which sounds blunt
(EN) Misreading Merci alone as acceptance (it often means no thanks when offered food)
boundaries: Suggesting outings among friends at A2 is kt:fr-fn-suggestions; written invitations are recognised in kt:fr-act-read-personal.

primitives.binding: Invitation dialogue with branches: accept, refuse with excuse, propose another day
Invite a friend and a colleague; adjust tu/vous and the formality of refusals

kcs.label: Congratulating, wishing and complimenting
kcs.description: Set phrases for congratulations, good wishes on occasions, and simple compliments, with suitable replies.
forms: Bravo ! / Félicitations !
Bon anniversaire ! / Bonne année ! / Joyeux Noël ! / Bonnes vacances ! / Bon appétit ! / Bonne chance !
Bon courage ! / Bon week-end !
compliments: C'est très joli ! / Tu es très élégant(e) ! / C'est délicieux !
replies: Merci ! / C'est gentil.

examples.fr: Bon anniversaire, Clara ! – Merci, c'est gentil !
examples.en: Happy birthday, Clara! – Thank you, that's kind!

examples.fr: Félicitations pour ton examen !
examples.en: Congratulations on your exam!

mastery: Matches wishes to occasions (birthday, exam, meal, departure)
Writes a birthday or holiday greeting card
Responds to a compliment and compliments a host on a meal
commonErrors: (EN) Translating "happy birthday" as *Heureux anniversaire (say Bon anniversaire or Joyeux anniversaire)
(EN) Saying Bonne chance when Bon courage fits (effort rather than luck)

primitives.binding: Judge which wish fits each occasion (bon courage / bonne chance / bon appétit); classify misuse; write a card
Party: compliment the host, wish happy birthday, reply to a compliment

kcs.label: Linking words: et, ou, mais, alors
kcs.term: Les articulateurs : et, ou, mais, alors
kcs.description: The first connectors to join words and short sentences: et (and, adding), ou (or, alternative), mais (but, contrast), alors (so, consequence in speech). They let A1 speakers produce two-clause sentences.
forms: et: J'ai un frère et une sœur.
ou: Du thé ou du café ?
mais: Il est petit mais très fort.
alors: Il pleut, alors je prends le bus.
ou vs où: ou = or, où = where

examples.fr: J'aime le sport mais je n'aime pas courir.
examples.en: I like sport but I don't like running.

examples.fr: Le bus ne passe pas, alors on prend un taxi.
examples.en: The bus isn't coming, so we're taking a taxi.

mastery: Chooses et / ou / mais / alors to join two clauses
Writes ou and où correctly
Joins short sentences in a description using all four connectors
commonErrors: (EN) Writing où for "or"
(EN) Using alors at the start like English "then" in a sequence (puis/ensuite is better)
boundaries: Cause with parce que is kt:fr-g-cause; A2 connectors are kt:fr-dis-connectors-a2; chronological connectors are kt:fr-dis-chronological.

primitives.binding: Stop at et / mais / alors in a short text; learner predicts the direction of the next clause, then checks
Join pairs of sentences with the connector that fits the intended meaning

kcs.label: Partitive articles: du, de la, de l', des
kcs.description: Partitive articles express an unspecified amount of something uncountable (or treated as a mass): du pain, de la confiture, de l'eau. They are required where English uses 'some' or nothing. Compare: Je mange du fromage (some cheese) / J'aime le fromage (cheese in general) / Je prends un fromage (one cheese).
forms: du (m.), de la (f.), de l' (before vowel), des (pl.)
Je bois du café / de l'eau / de la limonade.
after negation → de: Je ne bois pas de café (kt:fr-g-pas-de)
with likes → definite article: J'aime le café.
with faire: faire du sport (kt:fr-lex-leisure)

examples.fr: Au petit déjeuner, je prends du pain, du beurre et de la confiture.
examples.en: For breakfast I have bread, butter and jam.

examples.fr: Tu veux de l'eau ? – Oui, je veux bien.
examples.en: Do you want some water? – Yes please.

mastery: Chooses du / de la / de l' / des by gender and initial sound
Chooses between partitive, definite and indefinite article according to meaning
Orders breakfast or a picnic list using partitives
commonErrors: (EN) Omitting the article (*Je mange pain)
(EN) *J'aime du chocolat (general taste uses le)
(EN) *de le pain (contract to du)
boundaries: Quantities with de (un kilo de) are kt:fr-g-quantity.

primitives.binding: Sort foods by how they are measured (du/de la mass vs un/une countable), induce the rule, then handle items that can be both (un café / du café)
Same food in three intents (general taste, some, one portion); learner picks le / du / un and sees the meaning change

kcs.label: Expressions of quantity and measurement
kcs.description: Quantities are followed by de/d' and no article: un kilo de pommes, une bouteille d'eau, beaucoup de monde, un peu de sel, assez de temps, trop de bruit. Also measurement phrases with à and numbers (à 10 km, moins 10 %).
forms: un kilo / 500 grammes / un litre / une bouteille / une boîte / une tranche / un morceau + de
beaucoup de, un peu de, assez de (A2), trop de, peu de (A2)
combien de … ? – deux kilos.
distances and reductions: à 10 km, moins 10 %, un mètre de large

examples.fr: Je voudrais un kilo de tomates et deux tranches de jambon.
examples.en: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes and two slices of ham.

examples.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde au marché aujourd'hui.
examples.en: There are a lot of people at the market today.

mastery: Selects the correct form after quantity words (de, never du/des)
Writes a shopping list with containers and weights
Buys three items at a market stall stating quantities
commonErrors: (EN) *un kilo des pommes / *beaucoup des amis
(EN) *beaucoup de le temps
(EN) Using *plusieurs for uncountables
boundaries: Partitive articles are kt:fr-g-partitive; the pronoun en with quantities is kt:fr-g-pronoun-en.

primitives.binding: Match foods to containers/units (une bouteille de, une boîte de, un kilo de), induce the "de + no article" rule
Market dialogues: note item, quantity and unit in a grid; errors classed by unit type

kcs.label: Polite conditional: je voudrais, j'aimerais, on pourrait
kcs.description: A handful of conditional forms used as polite requests and wishes, learned as chunks: je voudrais, j'aimerais, on pourrait, vous pourriez, tu pourrais. They soften je veux, which sounds demanding in a shop.
forms: Je voudrais + noun / infinitive
J'aimerais + infinitive
Vous pourriez / Pourriez-vous + infinitive … ?
On pourrait avoir … ?
Tu pourrais m'aider ?

examples.fr: Je voudrais un billet pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît.
examples.en: I'd like a ticket to Lyon, please.

examples.fr: On pourrait avoir l'addition, s'il vous plaît ?

mastery: Chooses je voudrais over je veux in service situations
Turns direct requests into polite ones with pourriez-vous
Makes three polite requests in a hotel role-play

(EN) *Je voudrais à partir
boundaries: The full conditional paradigm is B1 (not covered).

primitives.binding: Same request to a friend, a waiter and an official; learner adjusts je veux / je voudrais / pourriez-vous
Choose request forms by intent (demand, polite request, wish) and see the effect on the listener

kcs.label: Shopping, prices and paying
kcs.term: Faire des achats, demander des prix
kcs.description: Simple transactions: asking for an item, asking the price, understanding the amount, paying by card or cash, and reading price labels, receipts and promotions.
forms: Je voudrais … / Vous avez … ? / Je cherche …
C'est combien ? / Ça coûte combien ? / Ça fait combien ?
Ça fait 12,50 € (douze euros cinquante).
Je peux payer par carte ? / en espèces
Et avec ceci ? – C'est tout, merci.
labels: prix, promotion, -20 %, soldes, le ticket de caisse

Completes a purchase from greeting to payment in a role-play

(EN) *Combien est-ce ? word order
(EN) Not greeting the shopkeeper before asking
boundaries: Restaurant ordering is kt:fr-fn-restaurant; complaints at A2 are kt:fr-fn-complain.

Receipts, price labels and promo flyers: find the total, the reduction and the unit price

kcs.label: Prepositions of place and contractions
kcs.term: Les prépositions de lieu : à, au, de, chez, dans…
kcs.description: Prepositions to locate people and things and to say where one goes: à (with contraction au/aux), de (du/des), chez + person, dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière, à côté de, en face de, avec.

de: Je viens du marché (de + le) / de la poste

kcs.label: The imperative
kcs.description: Commands and instructions use the present-tense forms of tu, nous and vous without the subject: Prends ! Prenons ! Prenez ! For -er verbs the tu form drops the -s (Regarde !). Irregular: être (sois, soyez), avoir (aie, ayez). Negative: Ne … pas around the verb. Used for directions, recipes, instructions.
forms: tu: Regarde ! Viens ! Prends la première rue.
vous: Tournez à gauche. Ouvrez vos livres.
nous: Allons-y !
negative: Ne touche pas ! Ne parlez pas.
être/avoir: Sois sage ! Ayez votre billet.

examples.fr: Prenez la deuxième rue à droite, puis continuez tout droit.
examples.en: Take the second street on the right, then carry straight on.

examples.fr: Ne cours pas, attends-moi !
examples.en: Don't run, wait for me!

mastery: Carries out spoken classroom and street instructions
Converts tu ↔ vous imperatives including the dropped -s
Gives a sequence of instructions (directions, recipe)
commonErrors: (EN) Keeping the subject (*Vous tournez à gauche ! is a statement)
(EN) *Regardes ! (-er tu form without -s)
(EN) Using the imperative with strangers without s'il vous plaît
boundaries: Pronoun placement with imperatives (dis-moi) appears in kt:fr-g-indirect-object-pronouns.

primitives.binding: Hear imperatives and drag the character along a map or perform classroom actions
Derive the imperative from present forms of unseen verbs; the rule step (drop subject, drop -s) is shown

kcs.label: Asking for and giving directions
kcs.description: Asking how to get somewhere, understanding simple directions and giving them using imperatives, ordinal numbers and place prepositions; reading simple maps and signs.
forms: Pour aller à …, s'il vous plaît ? / Où est … ?
Allez / Va tout droit; tournez à gauche / à droite; prenez la première / deuxième rue
traversez la place, continuez jusqu'au feu / au carrefour
C'est loin ? – C'est à cinq minutes à pied.
C'est sur votre gauche / en face de …

examples.fr: Pour aller à la gare, s'il vous plaît ? – Allez tout droit, puis prenez la deuxième à gauche.
examples.en: How do I get to the station? – Go straight on, then take the second on the left.

examples.fr: C'est à dix minutes à pied, en face du musée.
examples.en: It's ten minutes' walk, opposite the museum.

mastery: Traces a route on a map from heard directions
Gives directions between two points on a map
Asks for and follows directions in a role-play, checking understanding
commonErrors: (EN) Confusing tout droit (straight on) and à droite (on the right)
(EN) *Tournez le gauche
(EN) *la deuxième rue sur la gauche (à gauche)
boundaries: Means of transport are kt:fr-lex-transport.

primitives.binding: Hear directions and drag a pin along a street map; the path itself is the evidence
One partner has the destination marked; the other must ask for and follow directions

kcs.label: Means of transport and using them
kcs.description: Vehicles and the prepositions that go with them (en bus, à pied), plus the vocabulary for buying tickets and using public transport.
forms: en voiture, en bus, en train, en métro, en avion, en taxi
à pied, à vélo (en vélo in speech), à moto
prendre le bus / le train; monter dans, descendre de
un billet, un aller simple, un aller-retour, un ticket de métro, composter / valider

examples.en: A return ticket to Bordeaux, please.

Buys a train ticket and asks about the platform

(EN) *en pied (à pied)
(EN) *monter le bus / *sortir le train (monter dans le bus, descendre du train)

primitives.binding: Departure board and train ticket: find platform, car number, departure time
Ticket office: buy an aller-retour, branches for no seats and change of time

kcs.label: Asking about and describing places
kcs.description: Asking what a place is like and describing a town, neighbourhood, house or landscape: location, size, what there is, and evaluation.
forms: C'est comment, Lille ? / Comment est ton quartier ?
C'est une grande ville / un petit village; c'est calme, animé, joli, moderne
Il y a beaucoup de … / Il n'y a pas de …
C'est situé près de … / au bord de la mer (A2)

examples.fr: Mon quartier est calme ; il y a un parc et deux écoles.
examples.en: My neighbourhood is quiet; there's a park and two schools.

examples.fr: Comment est la plage ? – Elle est petite mais très belle.
examples.en: What's the beach like? – It's small but very beautiful.

mastery: Matches spoken descriptions to photos of places
Writes a five-sentence description of own town
Asks a partner about their town and compares
commonErrors: (EN) *C'est une ville grande (position)
(EN) Using il est to describe a place mentioned with c'est
boundaries: Presenting a country and its people at A2 is kt:fr-fn-present-country.

primitives.binding: Photo of a town square; learner describes it; checker verifies what is there and where
Start from "Ma ville est petite" and expand step by step with il y a, adjectives and location

kcs.label: Near future: aller + infinitive
kcs.description: Aller in the present + infinitive expresses plans and things about to happen. It is the most frequent way to talk about the future in speech. Negation surrounds aller.
forms: je vais partir, tu vas voir, il va pleuvoir
nous allons manger, vous allez aimer, ils vont arriver
negative: Je ne vais pas sortir.
with time words: demain, ce soir, la semaine prochaine

examples.fr: Ce week-end, je vais aller à la montagne.
examples.en: This weekend I'm going to go to the mountains.

examples.fr: Attention, le train va partir !
examples.en: Careful, the train is about to leave!

mastery: Distinguishes je vais + place and je vais + infinitive
Transforms present sentences into futur proche, including negatives
Describes three plans for next weekend
commonErrors: (EN) Conjugating both verbs (*je vais pars)
(EN) *Je ne vais partir pas
(EN) *Je vais à partir
boundaries: Futur simple is kt:fr-g-futur-simple.

primitives.binding: Place events before/after "now"; pick futur proche for planned events on the right of the line
Apply aller + infinitive to new verbs and subjects; the system shows the two-part rule

kcs.label: Recent past: venir de + infinitive
kcs.description: Venir in the present + de + infinitive says that something has just happened: Je viens de manger (I've just eaten).
forms: je viens de, tu viens de, il vient de, nous venons de, vous venez de, ils viennent de + infinitive
de → d' before a vowel: Il vient d'arriver.
contrast with venir de + place: Je viens de Lyon.

examples.fr: Désolé, le bus vient de partir.
examples.en: Sorry, the bus has just left.

examples.fr: Nous venons d'arriver à l'hôtel.
examples.en: We've just arrived at the hotel.

mastery: Distinguishes venir de + infinitive (just done) from venir de + place
Describes what people in pictures have just done
Explains a situation with venir de (je viens de perdre mes clés)
commonErrors: (EN) Translating "I have just" with *J'ai juste mangé
(EN) *Je viens manger (missing de changes the meaning)
boundaries: Passé composé is kt:fr-g-pc-avoir.

primitives.binding: Mark an event just before "now" vs earlier; choose venir de or passé composé
Pictures of results (empty plate, wet umbrella): learner says what has just happened; checked against scene

kcs.label: Être en train de + infinitive
kcs.description: Être en train de + infinitive stresses that an action is in progress right now. It is optional: the simple present can also describe a current action, and en train de is mainly used for emphasis or contrast.
forms: je suis en train de travailler
Qu'est-ce que tu es en train de faire ?
negative: Je ne suis pas en train de dormir !

examples.fr: Je ne peux pas parler, je suis en train de conduire.
examples.en: I can't talk, I'm driving.

examples.fr: Les enfants sont en train de jouer dans le jardin.
examples.en: The children are playing in the garden.

mastery: Recognises en train de as an ongoing action
Describes what people in a picture are doing at this moment
Explains on the phone why they cannot do something now
commonErrors: (EN) Overusing en train de for every present action
(EN) *Je suis travailler / *Je suis travaillant
boundaries: Present tense forms are kt:fr-g-present-er and kt:fr-g-present-irregular.

primitives.binding: Mark actions as ongoing at "now" vs habitual; choose en train de only for the ongoing slot
Busy park picture: say what five people are doing right now; checked against the scene

kcs.label: Talking about plans
kcs.description: Asking about and describing plans for the near future (weekend, holidays, after school), using the futur proche, the present with a future time phrase, and vouloir / avoir envie de.
forms: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce week-end ? / Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire cet été ?
Samedi, je vais … / Demain, je pars à …
J'ai envie de … / Je voudrais …
la semaine prochaine, le mois prochain, dans deux jours

examples.fr: Cet été, je vais travailler un mois, puis je pars en Grèce.
examples.en: This summer I'm going to work for a month, then I'm off to Greece.

examples.fr: Ce soir, j'ai envie de rester à la maison.
examples.en: Tonight I feel like staying at home.

mastery: Understands the plans of two speakers and notes what each will do
Writes a short message describing weekend plans
Describes holiday plans and preparations in a short monologue
commonErrors: (EN) Using the present without a time marker so the plan is unclear
(EN) *dans la semaine prochaine
boundaries: Intentions and ambitions at A2 are kt:fr-fn-wishes-intentions.

primitives.binding: Use the plan language from a model text for the learner's own next weekend
Expand "Samedi, je vais à la plage" into a paragraph with who, how, and after

l'hôtel, le camping, l'auberge de jeunesse, la location

kcs.label: Il faut / il ne faut pas + infinitive
kcs.description: Impersonal il faut + infinitive states a general necessity (one must / you need to); il ne faut pas means 'you must not', not 'you don't have to'. Il faut + noun means 'you need'.
forms: Il faut + infinitive: Il faut réserver.
Il ne faut pas + infinitive: Il ne faut pas fumer ici.
Il faut + noun: Il faut un passeport.
contrast: Tu n'es pas obligé(e) de … (you don't have to)

examples.fr: Pour entrer au musée, il faut acheter un billet en ligne.
examples.en: To get into the museum, you have to buy a ticket online.

examples.fr: Il ne faut pas parler pendant le film.
examples.en: You mustn't talk during the film.

mastery: Interprets il ne faut pas as prohibition, not absence of obligation
Writes rules for a classroom or a campsite with il faut / il ne faut pas
Gives advice on preparing a trip
commonErrors: (EN) Reading il ne faut pas as "you don't need to"
(EN) *Il faut que + infinitive / *Je faut
(EN) *Il faut de partir
boundaries: Il faut que + subjunctive is recognised at A2 (kt:fr-g-il-faut-subjunctive); expressing obligation generally is kt:fr-fn-obligation.

primitives.binding: Ladder of obligation (il faut – il vaut mieux – tu peux – tu n'es pas obligé – il ne faut pas); choose a rung for each rule
Campsite and museum rules signs: find what is forbidden and what is required

kcs.label: Purpose: pour + infinitive / noun
kcs.description: Pour + infinitive expresses purpose ('in order to'); pour + noun expresses destination or beneficiary. English 'to' of purpose must be pour, not à.
forms: pour + infinitive: Je vais à la bibliothèque pour étudier.
pour + noun: un cadeau pour ma mère, le train pour Paris
Pourquoi ? – Pour …

examples.fr: C'est un cadeau pour toi !
examples.en: It's a present for you!

mastery: Chooses pour + infinitive for purpose
Answers pourquoi questions with pour + infinitive
Explains the reasons for three daily actions
commonErrors: (EN) *Je vais au marché à acheter du pain
(EN) *pour à + infinitive
boundaries: Cause (parce que) is kt:fr-g-cause; sans + infinitive is kt:fr-g-sans-infinitive.

primitives.binding: Join action + aim sentences with pour, or unpack a pour sentence into two
Same action with reason or aim; learner picks parce que or pour and sees the change

kcs.label: Cause: parce que, à cause de
kcs.term: La cause : parce que, à cause de
kcs.description: Parce que + clause gives a reason, typically answering pourquoi ?. At A2, à cause de + noun gives a (usually negative) cause. Parce que becomes parce qu' before a vowel.
forms: Pourquoi … ? – Parce que …
parce qu' + il/elle/on
à cause de + noun: à cause de la pluie, à cause du bruit (A2)
contrast: grâce à (positive cause) is B1

examples.fr: Je ne viens pas parce que je suis malade.
examples.en: I'm not coming because I'm ill.

examples.fr: Le match est annulé à cause de la neige.
examples.en: The match is cancelled because of the snow.

mastery: Answers pourquoi questions with parce que + clause
Chooses parce que (clause) or à cause de (noun)
Explains two decisions with reasons in a short text
commonErrors: (EN) *à cause que / *parce que la pluie
(EN) *parce que il
boundaries: Consequence (donc, c'est pour ça) is kt:fr-g-consequence; giving reasons as a function at A2 is kt:fr-fn-reasons.
kcs.placementNote: Annexe D shades parce que at A1 as « moins clé » and lists « parce que, à cause de » as key at A2; introduced at A1 because pourquoi/parce que is needed for basic exchanges.

primitives.binding: Give a reason as a clause or a noun; learner picks parce que / à cause de and sees the structure required
Join effect + cause sentences, then unpack a parce que sentence

kcs.label: Passé composé with avoir
kcs.description: The passé composé (present of avoir + past participle) narrates completed past events. Regular participles: -er → -é, -ir → -i, many -re → -u. A small set of frequent irregular participles is learned at A1 (fait, pris, eu, été, vu, bu, lu, dit, écrit, mis). Negation surrounds the auxiliary.
forms: j'ai parlé, tu as fini, il a vendu
irregular: faire → fait, prendre → pris, avoir → eu, être → été, voir → vu, boire → bu, lire → lu, dire → dit
negative: Je n'ai pas compris.
time markers: hier, la semaine dernière, l'année dernière, il y a deux jours

examples.fr: Hier, j'ai mangé au restaurant et j'ai vu un film.
examples.en: Yesterday I ate at a restaurant and saw a film.

examples.fr: Tu as fini ? – Non, je n'ai pas encore fini.
examples.en: Have you finished? – No, I haven't finished yet.

mastery: Recognises passé composé forms in a short text and says when the events happened
Forms the passé composé of regular verbs and ten irregular ones
Writes five sentences about last weekend
commonErrors: (EN) Omitting the auxiliary (*Je mangé)
(EN) *J'ai fais / *J'ai prendu
(EN) *Je n'ai mangé pas
(EN) Using passé composé only for "have done" and not for "did"
boundaries: Verbs with être are kt:fr-g-pc-etre; agreement with être is kt:fr-g-pc-agreement; contrast with the imparfait is kt:fr-g-pc-vs-imparfait.

primitives.binding: Put completed events to the left of "now" and form the passé composé for each
Derive participles (-é, -i, -u) for unseen regular verbs; irregular ones are flagged as exceptions

kcs.label: Passé composé with être (movement verbs)
kcs.description: About fifteen intransitive verbs of movement or change of state, and all pronominal verbs, form the passé composé with être: aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, rester, tomber, naître, mourir, retourner, devenir, revenir. At A1 a few are learned in context (je suis allé(e), je suis parti(e)); agreement is introduced and practised fully at A2.
forms: je suis allé(e), tu es venu(e), il est parti, elle est partie
nous sommes arrivé(e)s, vous êtes resté(e)(s), ils sont sortis
naître → né, mourir → mort
negative: Je ne suis pas sorti(e).

examples.fr: Samedi, je suis allée au marché, puis je suis rentrée.
examples.en: On Saturday I went to the market, then I went home. (female speaker)

examples.fr: Il est né en 2001 à Dakar.
examples.en: He was born in 2001 in Dakar.

mastery: Sorts verbs into avoir and être groups
Uses je suis allé(e), parti(e), rentré(e), resté(e) in a narrative
Says where they went and when they came back last weekend
commonErrors: (EN) *J'ai allé
(EN) *Je suis mangé (être with transitive verbs)
(EN) Translating "I was born" as *J'étais né
boundaries: Full agreement rules are kt:fr-g-pc-agreement (A2).

primitives.binding: Sort past-tense verbs into avoir / être boxes, induce the movement rule, then handle exceptions
Order pictures of a trip (partir, arriver, rester, rentrer) and retell in the passé composé

kcs.label: Il y a, depuis, dans: locating events in time
kcs.term: Les indicateurs de temps : il y a, depuis, dans
kcs.description: Three time indicators English speakers often confuse: il y a + duration = 'ago' (with a past tense); depuis + duration/date = 'for/since' with the present for something still true; dans + duration = 'in' (from now) for the future.
forms: il y a + duration (ago): Je suis arrivé il y a deux jours.
depuis + duration/date + present: J'habite ici depuis trois ans / depuis 2020.
dans + duration (future): Le train part dans dix minutes.
Depuis quand … ? / Depuis combien de temps … ?

examples.fr: J'apprends le français depuis six mois.
examples.en: I've been learning French for six months.

examples.fr: Je l'ai vu il y a une semaine ; je le revois dans deux jours.
examples.en: I saw him a week ago; I'm seeing him again in two days.

mastery: Places events on a timeline from sentences with il y a, depuis and dans
Chooses the right indicator and tense for an English prompt
Talks about how long they have lived somewhere and when they arrived
commonErrors: (EN) Using the passé composé with depuis for an ongoing situation (*J'ai habité ici depuis 3 ans)
(EN) *Il y a deux jours je arrive
(EN) Using en for "in" from now (*en dix minutes for a future point)
boundaries: Pendant and à partir de are kt:fr-g-time-a2.

primitives.binding: Draw each sentence on a timeline (point in past, span up to now, point in future) and choose il y a / depuis / dans
Sentence pairs J'habite ici depuis 3 ans / J'ai habité ici pendant 3 ans: judge whether the person still lives there

kcs.label: C'était + adjective: evaluating a past experience
kcs.description: C'était is the imparfait of c'est, learned at A1 as a chunk to comment on a past experience (C'était super !). The full imparfait comes at A2.
forms: C'était bien / super / génial / nul / intéressant / ennuyeux.
Il faisait beau. (weather, chunk)
C'était comment ? – C'était très sympa.

examples.fr: Tu as aimé le concert ? – Oui, c'était génial !
examples.en: Did you like the concert? – Yes, it was great!

examples.fr: Le voyage, c'était comment ? – C'était long mais intéressant.
examples.en: How was the trip? – Long but interesting.

mastery: Understands evaluations of past events in a dialogue
Comments on last weekend's activities with c'était + adjective
Asks C'était comment ? and responds
commonErrors: (EN) *C'est été bien / *Il était bien for an event
(EN) Using c'est for a finished experience
boundaries: Imparfait forms and uses are kt:fr-g-imparfait-forms and kt:fr-g-imparfait-description.

primitives.binding: Comment on the present (c'est) or a past event (c'était); learner chooses and sees the time reference change
Monday-morning chat about the weekend; partner asks C'était comment ? and branches

kcs.label: Saying what you did
kcs.description: Telling, in a few connected sentences, what one did (yesterday, last weekend, on holiday), with the passé composé, time markers and et / puis, and a short evaluation.
forms: Hier / Samedi dernier / Le week-end dernier, j'ai …
D'abord …, puis …, après …
C'était …
Qu'est-ce que tu as fait ce week-end ?

examples.fr: Samedi, j'ai fait les courses, puis je suis allé au cinéma avec Tom. C'était sympa.
examples.en: On Saturday I did the shopping, then went to the cinema with Tom. It was nice.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier soir ? – J'ai regardé un match à la télé.
examples.en: What did you do last night? – I watched a match on TV.

mastery: Understands a short spoken account of a weekend and orders the events
Writes four sentences about last weekend
Asks a partner about their weekend and reports two things
commonErrors: (EN) Telling the whole story in the present
(EN) Mixing avoir and être auxiliaries
boundaries: Longer narratives with imparfait are kt:fr-fn-narrate (A2).

primitives.binding: Order weekend pictures and retell with d'abord, puis, après and c'était
Write a weekend message, compare with a model, mark one gap, rewrite

kcs.label: Home: rooms, furniture and equipment
kcs.description: Types of housing, rooms, furniture and household equipment, and floors (in France the rez-de-chaussée is the ground floor and the premier étage is one floor up).
forms: un appartement, une maison, un studio; le loyer
la cuisine, le salon, la chambre, la salle de bains, les toilettes, le jardin, le balcon
un lit, une table, une chaise, un canapé, une armoire, une étagère
le frigo, la cuisinière, le lave-linge, la douche
au rez-de-chaussée, au premier étage, au deuxième étage

examples.fr: J'habite dans un deux-pièces au troisième étage.
examples.en: I live in a two-room flat on the third floor.

examples.fr: Dans ma chambre, il y a un lit, un bureau et une grande armoire.
examples.en: In my bedroom there is a bed, a desk and a big wardrobe.

mastery: Labels rooms and furniture on a floor plan
Describes own home in five sentences with il y a and prepositions
Understands a simple flat advertisement (pièces, étage, loyer)
commonErrors: (EN) Counting floors the British-American way (premier étage = first floor up)
(EN) Using pièce and chambre interchangeably (chambre = bedroom)
boundaries: Describing places generally is kt:fr-fn-describe-places; reading classified ads is in kt:fr-act-read-public.

primitives.binding: Floor plan: learner describes where things are; checked against the plan
Show a visitor around the flat room by room, then show a different flat

kcs.label: Jobs and the world of work
kcs.term: Le monde du travail, les métiers
kcs.description: Names of common jobs with their feminine forms, workplaces, and A2 vocabulary of work (colleagues, hours, salary, contract).
forms: professeur(e), médecin, infirmier / infirmière, vendeur / vendeuse, serveur / serveuse, ingénieur(e), avocat(e), étudiant(e), retraité(e)
Je suis + job (no article) / C'est un(e) + job
travailler dans un bureau / un magasin / un hôpital / une école
A2: un(e) collègue, le patron, le salaire, les horaires, un CDD / CDI, être au chômage

examples.fr: Ma mère est infirmière ; elle travaille dans un hôpital.
examples.en: My mother is a nurse; she works in a hospital.

examples.fr: Je suis étudiant, mais je travaille le week-end comme serveur.
examples.en: I'm a student, but I work weekends as a waiter.

mastery: Matches jobs to workplaces and feminine forms
States own job or studies and those of two relatives
At A2, describes a workplace (colleagues, hours)
commonErrors: (EN) *Je suis un professeur
(EN) Not making the feminine form (*Elle est vendeur)
boundaries: Talking about work experience at A2 is kt:fr-fn-work-experience.
Usage of feminine job titles (professeure, autrice) varies; France now accepts them, Québec adopted them earlier.

primitives.binding: Picture of a person at work → say the job with correct gender before reveal
Sort job nouns by how the feminine is formed (-e, -euse, -ière, same form), induce patterns, handle exceptions

kcs.label: Making, confirming and changing appointments
kcs.description: Fixing a time to meet (friend, doctor, hairdresser), confirming it, and at A2 moving it earlier or later or cancelling it politely.
forms: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous avec … / On se retrouve à quelle heure ?
Lundi à 10 h, ça vous va ? / C'est possible ?
Je confirme mon rendez-vous de mardi.
A2: Je dois annuler / reporter notre rendez-vous. / On peut avancer à 9 h ?
Désolé(e), je ne suis pas libre. Plutôt mercredi ?

examples.fr: Bonjour, je voudrais un rendez-vous avec le docteur Martin. – Jeudi à 15 h, ça vous va ?
examples.en: Hello, I'd like an appointment with Dr Martin. – Thursday at 3 pm, is that OK?

examples.fr: Je suis désolée, je dois annuler notre rendez-vous de demain.
examples.en: I'm sorry, I have to cancel our appointment tomorrow.

mastery: Notes the day and time of an appointment from a phone message
Writes a text message to move a meeting
Arranges an appointment by phone in a role-play, negotiating a time
commonErrors: (EN) Using rendez-vous only for romantic dates
(EN) *faire un rendez-vous (prendre rendez-vous)
boundaries: Times and dates are kt:fr-fn-telling-time and kt:fr-lex-dates; telephone conventions are kt:fr-fn-telephone.

primitives.binding: Booking with a receptionist; branches when proposed times are taken
Two diaries; partners must find a common slot by proposing and refusing times

kcs.label: Ça as a pronoun
kcs.description: Ça (short for cela) refers to a thing, an idea or a situation without naming it: Ça va ? Ça coûte combien ? J'aime ça. C'est ça. It is very frequent in speech; cela is its written equivalent.
forms: Ça va ? Ça marche ! Ça dépend.
Ça coûte combien ? / Ça fait 10 €.
J'aime ça. / Je n'aime pas ça.
C'est ça. / Ça, c'est mon livre.
cela / ceci in formal writing

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que c'est, ça ? – C'est un gâteau breton.
examples.en: What's that? – It's a Breton cake.

examples.fr: Tu aimes le jazz ? – Oui, j'adore ça !
examples.en: Do you like jazz? – Yes, I love it!

mastery: Understands ça in common chunks
Uses j'aime ça / ça coûte combien in context
Replaces a repeated idea with ça in short replies
commonErrors: (EN) Using le/la after aimer for general tastes where ça is natural (*Je l'aime for "I like it" about jazz)
(EN) Writing ça without cédille (*ca)
boundaries: Demonstrative pronouns celui/celle are kt:fr-g-demonstrative-pronouns (A2).

primitives.binding: Short dialogues: link each ça to what it refers to (a thing, a situation, a price)
Collect ça-chunks heard in a dialogue (ça va, ça marche, ça dépend) into a phrase bank and use one

kcs.label: On: we, people, someone
kcs.description: On takes a third-person singular verb but has three values: 'we' (very common in speech, replacing nous), 'people in general/they' (En France, on mange tard) and 'someone' (On a volé mon vélo). At A1 on = nous is the priority; the three values are key at A2.
forms: on + 3rd person singular verb: on va, on mange, on est
on = nous: On va au cinéma ce soir ?
on = people in general: Ici, on parle français.
on = someone: On a sonné. (A2)
agreement in writing with on = nous: On est partis. (accepted)

examples.fr: On se retrouve devant la gare à huit heures ?
examples.en: Shall we meet in front of the station at eight?

examples.fr: Au Québec, on dit « char » pour « voiture » dans la langue familière.
examples.en: In Québec people say "char" for "car" in informal speech.

mastery: Identifies which meaning on has in sentences
Converts nous sentences into on sentences with the right verb form
Makes suggestions with on (On va … ?) in a role-play
commonErrors: (EN) *On allons / *on sommes
(EN) Reading on always as "one", which sounds stiff in translation
boundaries: Subject pronouns are kt:fr-g-subject-pronouns; spoken register is kt:fr-soc-spoken-register.

primitives.binding: Sentences where only context shows whether on = we, people or someone; learner chooses the meaning
Rewrite nous forms with on, applying the 3rd-person singular rule

kcs.label: Conventions of informal letters, cards and emails
kcs.term: Les rituels de la lettre amicale et du courriel
kcs.description: Openings, closings and conventions of messages to friends and family: postcards, invitations, emails and text messages.
forms: Cher Paul, / Chère Anna, / Salut Léa ! / Coucou ! (very informal)
Je t'écris de … / Merci pour ton message.
closings: Bises / Bisous / Grosses bises / À bientôt / Amitiés
Signature: Ton ami(e) …
texting: slt, mdr, stp, bcp (recognition only)

examples.fr: Chère Mamie, je t'écris de Nice. Il fait beau ! Grosses bises, Lucas.
examples.en: Dear Grandma, I'm writing from Nice. The weather is lovely! Big kisses, Lucas.

examples.fr: Salut Tom, merci pour ton invitation ! À samedi, bises.
examples.en: Hi Tom, thanks for the invitation! See you Saturday, love.

mastery: Identifies opening and closing formulas in a postcard and an email
Chooses cher/chère and closings by relationship
Writes a postcard of 30–40 words to a friend
commonErrors: (EN) *Cher Anna (agreement)
(EN) Using Bises with a teacher or an official
(EN) Ending with a calque of "Best regards" in an informal note
boundaries: Formal letters are kt:fr-soc-formal-letter (A2).

primitives.binding: Postcard and email templates where each slot (opening, news, closing) constrains what goes there
Same message to a friend, a grandparent and a teacher; adjust opening and closing

kcs.label: Reading postcards, invitations and personal messages
kcs.description: Understanding short personal texts: postcards, invitations, notes, text messages and simple personal emails — who writes, what happened or is planned, when and where.
forms: text types: carte postale, invitation, faire-part, petit mot, SMS, courriel
key information: qui ? quoi ? quand ? où ? réponse demandée ?
formulas: RSVP / Merci de répondre avant le …
informal spelling in SMS recognised (stp, bcp, rdv)

examples.fr: Fête d'anniversaire samedi 12 à 19 h chez moi. Réponds-moi avant jeudi ! Marie
examples.en: Birthday party Saturday the 12th at 7 pm at my place. Reply before Thursday! Marie

examples.fr: Rdv 18h devant le ciné ? Bises
examples.en: Meet at 6 pm in front of the cinema? Love

mastery: Finds event, date, time and place in an invitation
Answers questions about a postcard (where, weather, activities)
Replies appropriately to an invitation or message read
commonErrors: (EN) Misreading the date format (12/03 = 12 March)
(EN) Missing the reply deadline formula
boundaries: Conventions for writing them are kt:fr-soc-informal-letter; writing replies is kt:fr-act-write-messages.

primitives.binding: Invitation, postcard and SMS thread: find the information needed to reply (date, place, deadline)
In a short email, link pronouns and on to the people they refer to

kcs.label: Writing short notes, lists and messages
kcs.term: Écrire des listes, notes et messages
kcs.description: Producing short functional texts: a shopping list, a note for a flatmate, a text message, a simple email or postcard of a few sentences joined with et, mais, alors.
forms: liste: 1 kg de pommes, 2 baguettes…
petit mot: Je suis au marché, je rentre à midi. Léo
SMS / courriel: greeting + 2–4 sentences + closing
connectors et, mais, alors, parce que

examples.fr: Salut ! Je suis chez Paul. Je rentre vers 20 h. Il y a des pâtes dans le frigo. Bises
examples.en: Hi! I'm at Paul's. I'll be back around 8. There's pasta in the fridge. Love

examples.fr: Liste : du lait, six œufs, un kilo de tomates, du fromage.
examples.en: List: milk, six eggs, a kilo of tomatoes, cheese.

mastery: Writes a shopping list with quantities
Writes a note giving where they are and when they will be back
Writes a 40-word message to a friend with greeting, news and closing
commonErrors: (EN) Writing English-style capitals on days and months
(EN) Missing accents and elision in short notes
boundaries: Letter conventions are kt:fr-soc-informal-letter; A2 emails and blogs are kt:fr-act-write-a2.

primitives.binding: Note, list and SMS templates where each slot constrains what is written
Write the note first, then compare with a model and fix one gap

kcs.label: Reading signs, notices and simple public texts
kcs.description: Finding the key information in short public texts: notices, posters, small ads, warning signs, information sheets and notes, especially when supported by pictures.
forms: signs: Entrée / Sortie, Poussez / Tirez, Fermé, Interdit de fumer, Attention
posters and notices: date, heure, lieu, prix, entrée libre
small ads: À louer, À vendre, 2 pièces, 600 €/mois
note de service: Réunion lundi 9 h, salle 3

examples.fr: À louer : studio meublé, 25 m², centre-ville, 550 € par mois.
examples.en: To let: furnished studio, 25 m², town centre, €550 a month.

examples.fr: Piscine fermée le lundi. Entrée gratuite pour les moins de 6 ans.
examples.en: Pool closed on Mondays. Free entry for under-sixes.

mastery: Matches signs to their meaning
Finds date, price and place on a poster
Chooses the right flat from three small ads for given needs
commonErrors: (EN) Confusing Poussez (push) and Tirez (pull)
(EN) Reading À louer as "to praise" (louer = rent)
boundaries: Directions signs are in kt:fr-fn-directions; tourist documents are kt:fr-act-read-tourist.

primitives.binding: Real-style notices, posters and flat ads: find the one line needed for a task
Mark blocking words in an ad; decide to guess (from picture, number) or look up

programme: date, heure, lieu, artiste, réservation

kcs.label: Understanding announcements, messages and instructions
kcs.description: Picking out the main information in short, slow, clear public announcements (station, shop, camp), voicemail messages and recorded instructions: what, when, where, what to do.
forms: station: Le train … à destination de … partira voie 3.
shop: Le magasin va fermer dans dix minutes.
voicemail: C'est … , rappelle-moi au …
recorded: Tapez 1. / Veuillez patienter.

examples.fr: Le TGV 6123 à destination de Marseille partira à 10 h 12, voie B.
examples.en: TGV 6123 to Marseille will depart at 10:12 from platform B.

examples.fr: Salut, c'est Inès. On se retrouve à 19 h au café ? Rappelle-moi !
examples.en: Hi, it's Inès. Shall we meet at 7 at the café? Call me back!

mastery: Notes destination, time and platform from a station announcement
Notes caller, purpose and callback number from a voicemail
Follows a camp loudspeaker announcement (where to go and when)
commonErrors: (EN) Missing numbers said in the 24-hour clock
(EN) Confusing voie (platform) with voix
boundaries: Numbers and times are kt:fr-lex-numbers-70-plus and kt:fr-fn-telling-time.

primitives.binding: Announcements and voicemails: fill fixed slots (destination, time, platform, number); review errors by type
Write what was heard of a voicemail, then align with the transcript to see what was lost

kcs.label: Following short everyday conversations and simple accounts
kcs.term: Comprendre des conversations et des récits courts
kcs.description: Following very short, slow conversations on familiar topics (family, shopping, free time) and very short simple spoken accounts, with the support of context and repetition.
forms: social conversations: greetings, introductions, plans
service conversations: shop, café, station
short account: what someone did, a simple anecdote
support: repetition, gestures, pictures

examples.fr: – Tu viens samedi ? – Je ne sais pas, je travaille. – Dommage !
examples.en: – Are you coming on Saturday? – I don't know, I'm working. – Too bad!

examples.fr: Hier, j'ai perdu mon chat. Je l'ai cherché partout, et il était dans l'armoire !
examples.en: Yesterday I lost my cat. I looked everywhere, and he was in the wardrobe!

mastery: Identifies the topic and the speakers' relationship in a short dialogue
Answers who / what / when questions about a heard conversation
At A2, follows a short discussion on a familiar topic and notes each speaker's view
commonErrors: (EN) Trying to understand every word instead of the main point
(EN) Missing negation when ne is dropped (je sais pas)
boundaries: Discussions (A2) are a revisit of this KC; media listening is kt:fr-act-listen-media.

primitives.binding: Write what was heard, then align with the transcript; see where dropped ne and liaison hid words
Pause a dialogue at a connector or question; predict the reply, then hear it

kcs.label: Speaking for a short time about oneself
kcs.term: Monologue suivi : se présenter, raconter sa journée
kcs.description: Producing a short, prepared monologue of a few linked sentences: presenting oneself, one's family, one's day or a plan, with basic connectors and clear pronunciation.
forms: Je m'appelle … J'ai … ans. J'habite à …
Dans ma famille, il y a …
Le matin, je … Ensuite, … Le soir, …
connectors: et, mais, alors, parce que

examples.fr: Je m'appelle Ana, j'ai vingt ans et je suis étudiante en biologie. J'habite à Lyon avec deux amies.
examples.en: My name is Ana, I'm twenty and I study biology. I live in Lyon with two friends.

examples.fr: Le samedi, je fais du sport le matin et le soir je sors avec mes amis.
examples.en: On Saturdays I do sport in the morning and in the evening I go out with friends.

mastery: Delivers a prepared 30-second self-introduction intelligibly
Speaks for one minute about daily routine using connectors
At A2, describes plans and preparations for a trip in a short monologue
commonErrors: (EN) Long pauses filled with English "um" instead of euh
(EN) Listing sentences without any connector
boundaries: A2 presentations on a topic are kt:fr-fn-present-topic.

primitives.binding: Record the monologue, transcribe it, mark one problem category, re-record one sentence
Grow a one-sentence introduction into a 6-sentence monologue step by step

kcs.label: Using cognates and spotting false friends
kcs.description: English and French share thousands of related words (information, restaurant, possible, -tion/-ment/-ité endings). Using them speeds up reading; a short list of frequent false friends must be checked.
forms: transparent: le restaurant, la nation, important, la possibilité
patterns: -ité ↔ -ity (la société), -eux ↔ -ous (dangereux), -ment ↔ -ly (rapidement)
false friends: la librairie (bookshop), actuellement (currently), rester (stay), une location (rental), assister à (attend), sensible (sensitive)
pronunciation differs even when spelling is the same

examples.fr: C'est une situation très importante pour la société.
examples.en: It's a very important situation for society.

examples.fr: Actuellement, je reste chez ma tante.
examples.en: At the moment I'm staying at my aunt's.

mastery: Underlines cognates in a short text and guesses their meaning
Identifies false friends in sentences and gives the real meaning
Uses cognate patterns to understand a brochure faster
commonErrors: (EN) Reading actuellement as "actually"
(EN) Pronouncing cognates the English way (restaurant with final t)
boundaries: Guessing from context at A2 is kt:fr-str-guess-context.

primitives.binding: Write the meaning guessed from English for each word, then check usage; tag same / shifted / different
In a short text, decide which cognates are safe to guess and which need checking

kcs.label: Asking for and offering help
kcs.description: Asking someone for help and offering help, with the replies, using pouvoir and the polite conditional.
forms: Vous pouvez m'aider, s'il vous plaît ? / Tu peux m'aider ?
J'ai besoin d'aide.
Je peux vous aider ? / Je peux t'aider ? / Vous avez besoin d'aide ?
Oui, merci, c'est gentil. / Non merci, ça va.

examples.fr: Excusez-moi, vous pouvez m'aider ? Je ne trouve pas la sortie.
examples.en: Excuse me, can you help me? I can't find the exit.

examples.fr: Tu as besoin d'aide avec ta valise ? – Oui, merci !
examples.en: Do you need help with your suitcase? – Yes, thanks!

mastery: Recognises offers of help and replies appropriately
Asks for help in three situations (lost, heavy bag, form)
Offers help in a role-play and accepts/declines offers politely
commonErrors: (EN) *Vous pouvez aider moi ?

kcs.label: Punctuation and typographic conventions
kcs.description: French typography puts a (narrow) space before ? ! : ; and inside guillemets « », writes days, months and nationality adjectives in lower case, and uses a comma for decimals and a space for thousands.
forms: space before ? ! : ; → Tu viens ?
guillemets: « Bonjour »
lower case: lundi, janvier, français (adj.) vs les Français (people)
capital letters keep their accents in careful typography: À bientôt, État

examples.fr: Rendez-vous lundi 3 mars à 14 h 30 : salle B.
examples.en: Meeting Monday 3 March at 2.30 pm: room B.

examples.fr: Il a dit : « Je suis français. »
examples.en: He said: "I am French."

mastery: Spots English-style capitals and punctuation in a French text
Corrects punctuation, capitals and number formats in a short message
Writes a note or email with French typographic conventions
commonErrors: (EN) *Lundi 3 Mars (capitals on days/months)
(EN) *je suis Français (adjective takes lower case)
boundaries: Switzerland uses an apostrophe or space as thousands separator and often no space before ? !; Québec typography differs in the spaces before ? ! ;. Online informal writing often omits the space.

primitives.binding: Message with English typography: fix one convention at a time (spaces, capitals, numbers) and resubmit
Judge capitalisation of français / Français, lundi / Lundi in sentences; then write a sentence of each kind

citations.locator: CEFR 2001 §5.2.1.5 Orthographic competence
citations.note: L'Inventaire (§5, p. 14–15) présente des contenus clés « non exhaustifs » et ne détaille ni l'orthographe ni la prononciation (seul le scénario A2 « Partir en vacances » cite « liaisons, rythme, intonation »). French typography differs from English (no capitals on days, months, nationality adjectives; spacing before high punctuation in France).

kcs.label: Past participle agreement with être; pronominal verbs in the passé composé
kcs.term: Le participe passé et son accord (avec être)
kcs.description: With être the past participle agrees with the subject in gender and number (elle est partie, ils sont arrivés, elles sont venues). All pronominal verbs use être (je me suis levé(e)). Agreement is mostly silent but must be written; it is audible with some participles (mort/morte).
forms: elle est allée, nous sommes partis / parties, vous êtes venu(e)(s)
mixed group → masculine plural: Paul et Léa sont arrivés.
pronominal: je me suis réveillé(e), elle s'est habillée, nous nous sommes levés
negative: Elle ne s'est pas réveillée.
with on = nous: On est partis (accepted).

examples.fr: Mes cousines sont arrivées hier soir.
examples.en: My (female) cousins arrived last night.

examples.fr: Ce matin, je me suis levée à six heures.
examples.en: This morning I got up at six. (female speaker)

mastery: Chooses the correctly agreed participle for given subjects
Writes pronominal verbs in the passé composé with être and agreement
Writes a short account of a morning routine in the past with no auxiliary errors
commonErrors: (EN) Forgetting agreement because it is silent (*elle est parti)
(EN) *Je me ai levé / *J'ai me levé
(EN) Agreeing with avoir (*elle a mangée) — agreement with a preceding direct object is B1
boundaries: Agreement with avoir and a preceding direct object is B1, not covered.

primitives.binding: Apply the agreement rule to unseen subjects and verbs; the system shows subject gender → ending step by step
In own past-tense text, fix only auxiliary choice first, then only agreement

kcs.label: Sequencing connectors
kcs.description: Words that order events or points in a sequence: d'abord / tout d'abord, puis, ensuite, après, enfin / finalement, premièrement, deuxièmement. Used in narratives, instructions and short presentations.
forms: tout d'abord / d'abord
puis, ensuite, après (ça)
enfin, finalement
premièrement, deuxièmement (lists, arguments)
avant de + infinitive / après + noun (A2)

examples.fr: Premièrement, c'est trop cher ; deuxièmement, c'est loin.
